units.en: ShiftExample2Unsigned.c is trying to lay a simple truth on you and that truth is, you may see shifts in the assembly when no one wrote any shifts in the C So if a multiply by a power of 2 or a divide by a power of 2 exists in the C, then the compiler may just turn it into a shift left or a shift right. This particular assembly was compiled with a optimization Unlike all of our past,

units.en: which is 8, and divide by 16 This is a shift right by 2 to the power of 4, 16, and that's the only take away I have for you Multiplies and divides by powers of two compilers prefers shifts but you should still, as always, step through the assembly and check your understanding again If you'd like to make a little more complicated on yourself,
